503:  ## 1. OVERVIEW

505: +### Purpose
506: +
507: +Make the shared config surface visible before it changes a dispatch result, and name the flags that narrow what a dispatch can see.
508: +
509: +### When to Use
510: +
511: +- Deciding whether a dispatch can rely on the operator's editor configuration

514: +
515:  ### Core Principle

1: ---
2: title: cli-cursor
3: description: "Safe cross-AI dispatch into Cursor: sandboxed coding, Composer-model work, read-only plan or ask exploration and second-model opinions, all delivered through the `cursor-agent` CLI without leaving the calling runtime."
4: trigger_phrases:
5:   - "cursor"
6:   - "cursor cli"
7:   - "cursor agent"
8:   - "composer"
9:   - "delegate to cursor"
10:   - "second opinion"
11: version: 1.4.1.0
12: ---
13: 
14: # cli-cursor
15: 
16: > Cursor's own model can run the work while you stay in your current assistant. This skill makes that handoff safe and repeatable: sandboxed coding, Composer-model dispatch, read-only plan passes and read-only ask passes, all without leaving your runtime.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
21: 
22: | Aspect | What you get |
23: |---|---|
24: | **Use it for** | Sandboxed coding, Composer-model dispatch, read-only plan or ask exploration and cross-model validation through Cursor's `cursor-agent` CLI |
25: | **Invoke with** | "cursor", "cursor agent", "composer", "second opinion" or auto-routing on Cursor keywords |
26: | **Works on** | Any external runtime (Claude Code, Codex, raw shell) that needs to reach the `cursor-agent` binary |
27: | **Produces** | Code edits in a workspace, text responses and read-only plan or ask analyses |
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## 2. OVERVIEW
32: 
33: ### Why This Skill Exists
34: 
35: A non-Cursor assistant has no built-in way to reach the `cursor-agent` binary. When a task wants Cursor's own Composer model, a read-only plan or ask pass or a second AI opinion, the caller either hand-builds fragile `cursor-agent -p` invocations and picks flags by trial or skips the capability.
36: 
37: Two traps make naive dispatch dangerous:
38: 
39: - **The zero exit code.** `cursor-agent -p` exits `0` even when the account is not authenticated, so an exit-code check reports success on a dispatch that never reached a model.
40: - **The shared config surface.** The CLI also shares its config surface with the Cursor editor, so a dispatched session silently inherits editor-level hooks, MCP servers, rules and other configuration.
41: 
42: If the calling assistant is itself running inside Cursor CLI, a circular self-dispatch burns tokens for no value.
43: 
44: This skill standardizes the dispatch, runs a text-based auth pre-flight and guards against self-invocation so the caller never builds its own wrapper.
45: 
46: ### What It Does
47: 
48: cli-cursor is the single routing point for external runtimes that need Cursor CLI. A smart router scores the task against intent signals such as code generation, review, Composer dispatch, read-only plan or ask exploration and agent delegation, then loads only the references that match. It fails closed when `command -v cursor-agent` cannot resolve the binary. A self-invocation guard built from live-confirmed `CURSOR_AGENT` and `CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID` env signals plus process ancestry refuses to load when the caller is already inside Cursor CLI. Orchestrated execution delegates to the shipped deep-loop runtime, so this packet never builds a second adapter.
49: 
50: It does not write application code or manage spec folders. `sk-code` owns code standards and tests. `system-spec-kit` owns spec folders, memory and continuity. cli-cursor dispatches to Cursor and hands the result back to the caller.
51: 
52: ### The Dispatch Guard Rails
53: 
54: | Guard | What the skill knows how to operate |
55: |---|---|
56: | **Smart router** | Score task intent across code generation, review, Composer dispatch, read-only plan or ask exploration and agent delegation, then load only the matching references |
57: | **Model allowlist** | Enforce the exact 29 Cursor model ids across Composer, Gemini 3.8 Flash High, GLM 5.2, GPT-5.6 Luna Max and Grok (4.5, 4.6 and 4.7), rejecting `auto` and parameterized `model[effort=...]` brackets |
58: | **Auth pre-flight** | Read `cursor-agent about` output text and halt on "Not logged in" before the first dispatch |
59: | **Self-invocation guard** | Detect `CURSOR_AGENT` or `CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID` plus `cursor-agent` process ancestry, then refuse to load |
60: | **Memory handback** | Extract a live Cursor session's context in 7 steps and persist it through `generate-context.js` |
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ## 3. QUICK START
65: 
66: **Step 1: Verify the CLI is installed.**
67: 
68: ```bash
69: command -v cursor-agent
70: ```
71: 
72: If nothing prints, install it with `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash` and restart the terminal.
73: 
74: **Step 2: Run the default dispatch.**
75: 
76: ```bash
77: cursor-agent -p "Add input validation to src/utils.ts" \
78:   --output-format text \
79:   --model composer-2.5 \
80:   --auto-review \
81:   --sandbox enabled \
82:   2>&1
83: ```
84: 
85: The file is edited in place inside your workspace. For a read-only task such as exploration or Q&A, use `--mode plan` or `--mode ask` instead.
86: 
87: **Step 3: Reach for Composer when the task wants Cursor's own model.**
88: 
89: ```bash
90: cursor-agent -p "Review this diff for correctness" \
91:   --output-format text \
92:   --model composer-2.5 \
93:   --sandbox enabled \
94:   2>&1
95: ```
96: 
97: You get a response from Cursor's native model rather than a hosted frontier provider.
98: 
99: **Step 4: Run a read-only exploration pass.**
100: 
101: ```bash
102: cursor-agent -p "Explain how the auth flow works in this repo" \
103:   --mode ask \
104:   --model composer-2.5 \
105:   2>&1
106: ```
107: 
108: You get an analysis with no file writes. `--mode ask` and `--mode plan` are read-only regardless of approval flags.
109: 
110: ---
111: 
112: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
113: 
114: ### The Dispatch Lifecycle
115: 
116: The calling AI composes a prompt with the right model and approval mode. The shared deep-loop runtime constructs and runs the `cursor-agent` process. Cursor returns the result and the caller validates and integrates it. The packet owns routing and availability checks. `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs` owns execution.
117: 
118: ### The Two Silent Traps
119: 
120: Two Cursor CLI behaviors punish operators who do not know them. A reader who learns them here never hits them.
121: 
122: **Trap 1: the always-zero exit code.** `cursor-agent -p` returns exit code `0` even when the account is not authenticated. It prints `Error: Authentication required...` to output instead of failing the process. A naive `if [ $? -eq 0 ]` check reports success on a dispatch that never reached a model. Always inspect output text for an authentication error. Never trust the exit code alone.
123: 
124: **Trap 2: the shared editor config surface.** Unlike sibling CLIs with a tool-private config directory, Cursor CLI reads the exact same `.cursor/` and `~/.cursor/` files as the Cursor editor: `hooks.json`, `mcp.json`, `rules/` and any other file the editor keeps in that surface. A dispatched `cursor-agent` silently inherits the operator's editor-level hooks, MCP servers, rules and other configuration, which can surprise an orchestrator expecting a clean isolated session. See `references/shared-editor-config.md`.
125: 
126: ### The Self-Invocation Guard
127: 
128: If the agent reading this skill is itself running inside Cursor CLI, the skill refuses to load. The guard checks three layers in order:
129: 
130: 1. `CURSOR_AGENT=1`, which is set unconditionally whenever the current process runs under `cursor-agent` (confirmed live), plus `CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID` as the confirmed session-id marker.
131: 2. Process ancestry, where a `cursor-agent` parent in the tree trips the guard. The match runs against the canonical binary name, never the `agent` alias.
132: 3. A best-effort session probe in place of a lock file, since no lock-file convention is documented for Cursor CLI. This layer is weaker than the sibling packets' third layer and is documented as such.
133: 
134: When any layer matches, the skill returns a refusal and loads nothing. The cli-X family exists for cross-AI delegation. A running CLI skill never dispatches itself.
135: 
136: ### Model Selection And Execution Modes
137: 
138: Dispatch is scoped to an enforced 29-id allowlist. Cursor's own `auto` router is deliberately excluded, since it can silently resolve outside the set.
139: 
140: - **Composer** (`composer-2.5` and `composer-2.5-fast`) is Cursor's native model and the skill default. Those are Composer's only two tiers. It has no `-max` (1M-context "Max Mode") variant, so there is no Composer Max Mode to dispatch.
141: - **Gemini 3.8 Flash High** (`gemini-3.8-flash-high`) is the first Gemini id in the curated scope.
142: - **GLM 5.2** (`glm-5.2-high`, `glm-5.2-max`), **GPT-5.6 Luna Max** (`gpt-5.6-luna-max`, `gpt-5.6-luna-max-fast`), and **Grok** (4.5's 6 tiers `cursor-grok-4.5-{low,medium,high}[-fast]`, 4.6's 8 tiers `cursor-grok-4.6-{low,medium,high,xhigh}[-fast]` and 4.7's 8 tiers `grok-4.7-{low,medium,high,xhigh}[-fast]`) round out the allowlist.
143: - **Effort is part of the id.** Effort tiers are baked directly into a model id. There is no `--reasoning-effort` flag. The parameterized `model[effort=...]` bracket some sibling CLIs support is rejected outright by Cursor CLI.
144: 
145: Three execution modes govern how a dispatch behaves:
146: 
147: - The default agent mode (reads and writes, gated by approval flags)
148: - `--mode plan` (read-only planning)
149: - `--mode ask` (read-only Q&A)
150: 
151: Approval is a separate axis from the sandbox. `--auto-review` (Smart Auto) auto-runs safe actions and prompts for the rest. `--force` and `--yolo` (Run Everything) never prompt. Omitting both leaves Cursor's own default prompt-and-block behavior in place, which cannot proceed unattended.
152: 
153: ### Auth Pre-Flight And Memory Handback
154:

263: **Q: When do I pick Cursor over Codex or Claude Code?**
264: 
265: A: Reach for Cursor when the task specifically wants Composer, a read-only plan or ask pass or Cursor's unique worktree and cloud-worker surfaces. Reach for Codex for OpenAI-backed sandboxed coding and web research. Reach for Claude Code for deep extended thinking.

14: # cli-cursor
15: 
16: > Cursor's own model can run the work while you stay in your current assistant. This skill makes that handoff safe and repeatable: sandboxed coding, Composer-model dispatch, read-only plan passes and read-only ask passes, all without leaving your runtime.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
21: 
22: | Aspect | What you get |
23: |---|---|
24: | **Use it for** | Sandboxed coding, Composer-model dispatch, read-only plan or ask exploration and cross-model validation through Cursor's `cursor-agent` CLI |
25: | **Invoke with** | "cursor", "cursor agent", "composer", "second opinion" or auto-routing on Cursor keywords |
26: | **Works on** | Any external runtime (Claude Code, Codex, raw shell) that needs to reach the `cursor-agent` binary |
27: | **Produces** | Code edits in a workspace, text responses and read-only plan or ask analyses |
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## 2. OVERVIEW
32: 
33: ### Why This Skill Exists
34: 
35: A non-Cursor assistant has no built-in way to reach the `cursor-agent` binary. When a task wants Cursor's own Composer model, a read-only plan or ask pass or a second AI opinion, the caller either hand-builds fragile `cursor-agent -p` invocations and picks flags by trial or skips the capability.
36: 
37: Two traps make naive dispatch dangerous:
38: 
39: - **The zero exit code.** `cursor-agent -p` exits `0` even when the account is not authenticated, so an exit-code check reports success on a dispatch that never reached a model.
40: - **The shared config surface.** The CLI also shares its config surface with the Cursor editor, so a dispatched session silently inherits editor-level hooks, MCP servers, rules and other configuration.
41: 
42: If the calling assistant is itself running inside Cursor CLI, a circular self-dispatch burns tokens for no value.
43: 
44: This skill standardizes the dispatch, runs a text-based auth pre-flight and guards against self-invocation so the caller never builds its own wrapper.
45: 
46: ### What It Does
47: 
48: cli-cursor is the single routing point for external runtimes that need Cursor CLI. A smart router scores the task against intent signals such as code generation, review, Composer dispatch, read-only plan or ask exploration and agent delegation, then loads only the references that match. It fails closed when `command -v cursor-agent` cannot resolve the binary. A self-invocation guard built from live-confirmed `CURSOR_AGENT` and `CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID` env signals plus process ancestry refuses to load when the caller is already inside Cursor CLI. Orchestrated execution delegates to the shipped deep-loop runtime, so this packet never builds a second adapter.
49: 
50: It does not write application code or manage spec folders. `sk-code` owns code standards and tests. `system-spec-kit` owns spec folders, memory and continuity. cli-cursor dispatches to Cursor and hands the result back to the caller.
51: 
52: ### The Dispatch Guard Rails
53: 
54: | Guard | What the skill knows how to operate |
55: |---|---|
56: | **Smart router** | Score task intent across code generation, review, Composer dispatch, read-only plan or ask exploration and agent delegation, then load only the matching references |
57: | **Model allowlist** | Enforce the exact 29 Cursor model ids across Composer, Gemini 3.8 Flash High, GLM 5.2, GPT-5.6 Luna Max and Grok (4.5, 4.6 and 4.7), rejecting `auto` and parameterized `model[effort=...]` brackets |
58: | **Auth pre-flight** | Read `cursor-agent about` output text and halt on "Not logged in" before the first dispatch |
59: | **Self-invocation guard** | Detect `CURSOR_AGENT` or `CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID` plus `cursor-agent` process ancestry, then refuse to load |
60: | **Memory handback** | Extract a live Cursor session's context in 7 steps and persist it through `generate-context.js` |
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ## 3. QUICK START
65: 
66: **Step 1: Verify the CLI is installed.**
67: 
68: ```bash
69: command -v cursor-agent
70: ```
71: 
72: If nothing prints, install it with `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash` and restart the terminal.
73: 
74: **Step 2: Run the default dispatch.**
75: 
76: ```bash
77: cursor-agent -p "Add input validation to src/utils.ts" \
78:   --output-format text \
79:   --model composer-2.5 \
80:   --auto-review \
81:   --sandbox enabled \
82:   2>&1
83: ```
84: 
85: The file is edited in place inside your workspace. For a read-only task such as exploration or Q&A, use `--mode plan` or `--mode ask` instead.
86: 
87: **Step 3: Reach for Composer when the task wants Cursor's own model.**
88: 
89: ```bash
90: cursor-agent -p "Review this diff for correctness" \
91:   --output-format text \
92:   --model composer-2.5 \
93:   --sandbox enabled \
94:   2>&1
95: ```
96: 
97: You get a response from Cursor's native model rather than a hosted frontier provider.
98: 
99: **Step 4: Run a read-only exploration pass.**
100: 
101: ```bash
102: cursor-agent -p "Explain how the auth flow works in this repo" \
103:   --mode ask \
104:   --model composer-2.5 \
105:   2>&1
106: ```
107: 
108: You get an analysis with no file writes. `--mode ask` and `--mode plan` are read-only regardless of approval flags.
109:

111: 
112: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
113: 
114: ### The Dispatch Lifecycle
115: 
116: The calling AI composes a prompt with the right model and approval mode. The shared deep-loop runtime constructs and runs the `cursor-agent` process. Cursor returns the result and the caller validates and integrates it. The packet owns routing and availability checks. `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs` owns execution.
117: 
118: ### The Two Silent Traps
119: 
120: Two Cursor CLI behaviors punish operators who do not know them. A reader who learns them here never hits them.
121: 
122: **Trap 1: the always-zero exit code.** `cursor-agent -p` returns exit code `0` even when the account is not authenticated. It prints `Error: Authentication required...` to output instead of failing the process. A naive `if [ $? -eq 0 ]` check reports success on a dispatch that never reached a model. Always inspect output text for an authentication error. Never trust the exit code alone.
123: 
124: **Trap 2: the shared editor config surface.** Unlike sibling CLIs with a tool-private config directory, Cursor CLI reads the exact same `.cursor/` and `~/.cursor/` files as the Cursor editor: `hooks.json`, `mcp.json`, `rules/` and any other file the editor keeps in that surface. A dispatched `cursor-agent` silently inherits the operator's editor-level hooks, MCP servers, rules and other configuration, which can surprise an orchestrator expecting a clean isolated session. See `references/shared-editor-config.md`.
125: 
126: ### The Self-Invocation Guard
127: 
128: If the agent reading this skill is itself running inside Cursor CLI, the skill refuses to load. The guard checks three layers in order:
129: 
130: 1. `CURSOR_AGENT=1`, which is set unconditionally whenever the current process runs under `cursor-agent` (confirmed live), plus `CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID` as the confirmed session-id marker.
131: 2. Process ancestry, where a `cursor-agent` parent in the tree trips the guard. The match runs against the canonical binary name, never the `agent` alias.
132: 3. A best-effort session probe in place of a lock file, since no lock-file convention is documented for Cursor CLI. This layer is weaker than the sibling packets' third layer and is documented as such.
133: 
134: When any layer matches, the skill returns a refusal and loads nothing. The cli-X family exists for cross-AI delegation. A running CLI skill never dispatches itself.
135: 
136: ### Model Selection And Execution Modes
137: 
138: Dispatch is scoped to an enforced 29-id allowlist. Cursor's own `auto` router is deliberately excluded, since it can silently resolve outside the set.
139: 
140: - **Composer** (`composer-2.5` and `composer-2.5-fast`) is Cursor's native model and the skill default. Those are Composer's only two tiers. It has no `-max` (1M-context "Max Mode") variant, so there is no Composer Max Mode to dispatch.
141: - **Gemini 3.8 Flash High** (`gemini-3.8-flash-high`) is the first Gemini id in the curated scope.
142: - **GLM 5.2** (`glm-5.2-high`, `glm-5.2-max`), **GPT-5.6 Luna Max** (`gpt-5.6-luna-max`, `gpt-5.6-luna-max-fast`), and **Grok** (4.5's 6 tiers `cursor-grok-4.5-{low,medium,high}[-fast]`, 4.6's 8 tiers `cursor-grok-4.6-{low,medium,high,xhigh}[-fast]` and 4.7's 8 tiers `grok-4.7-{low,medium,high,xhigh}[-fast]`) round out the allowlist.
143: - **Effort is part of the id.** Effort tiers are baked directly into a model id. There is no `--reasoning-effort` flag. The parameterized `model[effort=...]` bracket some sibling CLIs support is rejected outright by Cursor CLI.
144: 
145: Three execution modes govern how a dispatch behaves:
146: 
147: - The default agent mode (reads and writes, gated by approval flags)
148: - `--mode plan` (read-only planning)
149: - `--mode ask` (read-only Q&A)
150: 
151: Approval is a separate axis from the sandbox. `--auto-review` (Smart Auto) auto-runs safe actions and prompts for the rest. `--force` and `--yolo` (Run Everything) never prompt. Omitting both leaves Cursor's own default prompt-and-block behavior in place, which cannot proceed unattended.

247: **Q: Why not just call `cursor-agent -p` directly from my shell?**

252: 
253: A: Pick `composer-2.5` or `composer-2.5-fast` (the default) when the task specifically wants Cursor's own house model or when no other model is named. 230: 8. Route to `--mode plan`/`--mode ask`/default agent per the task type (see Section 3 routing table).
231: 9. **Pass the spec folder to the delegated agent** in the prompt: if the calling AI has an active Gate-3 spec folder, include `Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)`. If none, ASK the user before delegating — the delegated agent cannot answer Gate 3 in `--force`/non-interactive mode.
232: 10. **Prompt construction & model-craft (cli-* family precedence).** Compose every dispatch prompt via the 2-tier rule canonical in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md`:
233:    1. **Fast path (default).** Build from the local `assets/prompt-quality-card.md`, which delegates the framework table + CLEAR check to the canonical card.
234:    2. **Deep path (escalation).** Dispatch `@prompt-improver` via the Task tool (never load full `sk-prompt` inline) when any canonical **Tier 2** trigger applies — the trigger list lives in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` under "Tier 2 — Deep path"; do not re-enumerate it here.
235: 11. **Never inject user-level voice/personalization content into AI-orchestrated Cursor delegations.** Cursor CLI reads rules from `.cursor/rules`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and legacy `.cursorrules` automatically. When an AI delegates via `cursor-agent -p`, the calling AI's own voice rules govern the response — keep delegations focused on task/model/approval/(spec-folder pre-approval).
236: 12. **Code Standards Loading (surface-aware contract)** — When dispatching for code review or code generation, instruct the dispatched session to:
237:     1. Load `sk-code`.
238:     2. Let `sk-code` emit a surface tag matching the detected stack from markers and target files.
239:     3. Load the selected surface resources and run its verification commands.
240:     4. Add `code-review` only for formal findings-first review output.
241: 
242:     Fallback: if the surface cannot be determined confidently, ask for the runtime surface and verification command set.
243:     NEVER hardcode obsolete sibling code skills in dispatch prompts.
244: 13. **Design Standards Loading (measured-reference contract)** — When dispatching for design or UI work, instruct the dispatched session to:
245:     1. Load `sk-design-md-generator`.
246:     2. Extract a measured Style Reference DESIGN.md from the live source before building UI. Include named color tokens, type scale, components, and Quick-Start CSS/Tailwind.
247:     3. Build against those measured tokens and run the extraction's validate step to confirm hex/section fidelity.
248: 
249:     Fallback: if there is no live source to measure, ask for the reference URL or the exact tokens to build against.
250:     NEVER treat `mcp-figma` or `sk-design-md-generator` as a taste, visual-direction, or critique authority.
251:     The extraction measures real CSS; it does not judge design.
252: 14. **Pass the design reference manifest to the dispatched session** — when dispatching design or UI work, inline a `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST v1` block in the prompt.
253:     The child cannot resolve skill paths, so the manifest travels in the payload, not by reference.
254:     Include `styleReferenceExtracted` true, the live `source` that was measured, the measured design tokens / type scale / components the child must build against, `loadedFiles`, and `proofDemandBack`.
255:     If the manifest cannot be assembled because no Style Reference was extracted or no live source can be measured, ASK before launching the child rather than starting a silent design dispatch.
256:     The child returns the demanded proof, and the parent reconciles it on the return path.
257: 15. **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped).**
258:     - By default, launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family.
259:     - Wait for the dispatched agent's work to return and verify that outputs exist.
260:       Then SIGKILL only the dispatch THIS skill started. Capture its PID at launch with `cursor-agent -p ... & CURSOR_PID=$!`.
261:       Kill that PID directly and its own orphan children with `kill -9 "$CURSOR_PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$CURSOR_PID" 2>/dev/null`.
262:     - **Never use a blanket `pkill -9 -f "cursor-agent"` pattern.** It matches and kills EVERY running `cursor-agent` process on the machine, including the operator's unrelated Cursor sessions and the operator's own Cursor editor, since the CLI shares the binary family.
263:     - Launch the next dispatch, this skill or a sibling, only after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped.
264:     - **Within a deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research), the operator authorizes the whole multi-iteration session at the start.
265:       Iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration confirmation prompt.
266:     - **Exception (cross-skill parallel):** when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently.
267:       Still SIGKILL each by its own captured PID as its work returns.
268: 16. **Set `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` in the dispatched child's env and state the exemption in the prompt.**
269:     The variable makes the waiver true, but it does not make it observable.
270:     The reader being waived is a model, and a model cannot see an environment variable.
271:     A child given only the variable still stops to ask the documentation-scope question and writes nothing, at exit code zero.
272:     Copy the preamble from [`shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md`](../shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md) to the top of every non-interactive prompt.
273:     A session may be launched through the per-session worktree wrapper (`.skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh`).
274:     A dispatched `cursor-agent -p` is an orchestrated sub-session, not a new top-level session.
275:     It must SHARE the parent's worktree rather than allocate its own.
276:     This is distinct from Cursor's own native `-w` worktree flag, which this packet's default dispatch never passes.
277:     Pattern: `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 cursor-agent -p ... </dev/null`.
278:     This is harmless when the wrapper is not in use.
279:     See `.skilled/bin/README.md` → "Worktree session isolation".
280: 
281: 17. **Agent-persona injection (attach identity, not just the task).**
282:     Every dispatch composes `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}`, never a bare task.
283:     Resolve the persona from the ACTIVE runtime's agent directory per AGENTS.md §9:
284:     `.cursor/agents/<name>.md`, `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, `.skilled/agents/<name>.md`, and other runtime paths.
285:     Never hardcode one runtime.
286:     Map each subtask to the RIGHT agent, not one default:
287:     `code`→code, `review`→review, `design`→design, research→`deep-research`, and docs→`markdown`.
288:     **Cursor has a native file-convention subagent surface.**
289:     `.cursor/agents/*.md` and `.claude/agents/*.md` mirror all 13 canonical agents.
290:     Dispatch by naming the resolved subagent to satisfy the rule.
291:     On a bare `cursor-agent -p` that names no subagent, **INLINE** the persona block into the payload.
292:     Use the same in-payload pattern as the `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST` (Rule 14), because the child cannot resolve agent paths by reference.
293:     A persona-less dispatch runs the leaf as a generic assistant and silently drops the agent's tool-scope, verification gates, and output contract.
294:     The canonical contract is `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection".
295:     The native precedent is `orchestrate.md` "Agent Loading Protocol".
296:     Declare rare exceptions at the dispatch site: a native surface used, a focused summary for a small-context model, or a pure-mechanical command.
297: 
298: ### ⛔ NEVER
299: 
300: 1. Pass `-w`/`--worktree` or dispatch `cursor-agent worker` from orchestrated fan-out without explicit user approval — these are opt-in escape hatches documented in `references/cursor-tools.md`, not this packet's default dispatch behavior.
301: 2. Trust Cursor output blindly for security-sensitive code, send sensitive data (API keys, passwords, credentials) in prompts, or hammer the CLI with rapid sequential calls.
302: 3. Use Cursor for tasks where context is already loaded — direct action by the calling AI is faster.
303: 4. Assume Cursor output is correct without verification — cross-reference codebase and project standards.
304: 5. Build or maintain a packet-local Cursor execution adapter; the deep-loop runtime is the execution authority.
305: 6. Treat a `0` exit code as proof of a successful, authenticated dispatch — always inspect output text.
306: 7. Do not dispatch a `--model` value outside the enforced 29-id allowlist (§3 Model Selection), including `auto`.
307:    Do not silently substitute the closest-sounding allowed model instead of asking the user.
308:    The runtime layer enforces this through `CURSOR_SUPPORTED_MODELS`/`isCursorModelAllowed` in `executor-config.ts`.
309:    A hard-rejecting check also runs in `fanout-run.cjs`'s `buildCursorLineageCommand` and `dispatch-model.cjs`'s cli-cursor case.
310:    This rule states the same constraint for advisory/manual dispatches the runtime layer cannot see.
311: 
312: ### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
313: 
314: 1. Cursor CLI is not installed and user has not acknowledged (provide `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash`).
315: 2. `cursor-agent about` reports "Not logged in" and the user has not acknowledged running `cursor-agent login`.
316: 3. Cursor output conflicts with existing code patterns (present both perspectives; user decides).
317: 4. Task requests `cursor-agent worker` (cloud execution) or native worktree isolation (`-w`) as part of an orchestrated fan-out (describe the scope-creep risk; get explicit user approval).
318: 
319: ### Memory Handback Protocol
320: 
321: When you need to preserve session context from a Cursor CLI delegation, run the canonical procedure:
322: - Extract the `MEMORY_HANDBACK` section.
323: - Build structured JSON and scrub secrets.

331: printf '%s' "$JSON_PAYLOAD" | node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js --stdin [spec-folder]
332: ```

1: ---
2: name: cli-cursor
3: description: "Cursor CLI executor for cursor-agent coding, plan/ask read-only modes and worktree-isolated cloud worker dispatch."
4: allowed-tools: [Bash, Read, Glob, Grep]
5: version: 1.5.9.0
6: ---
7: 
8: # Cursor CLI Orchestrator - Cross-AI Task Delegation
9: 
10: > **CRITICAL — SELF-INVOCATION PROHIBITED**
11: >
12: > This skill dispatches to the Cursor CLI binary (`cursor-agent`). If the agent currently reading this skill is itself running inside `cursor-agent` (detection signals listed in [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md)), the skill MUST refuse to load and return the documented error message instead of generating any `cursor-agent` invocation.
13: >
14: > A running CLI skill never dispatches itself. The cli-X skills are for **cross-AI delegation only** — never self-invocation.
15: 
16: Orchestrate Cursor's terminal coding agent (`cursor-agent`) for tasks that benefit from a second AI perspective, Cursor's native model (Composer), read-only plan/ask exploration, or its unique worktree/cloud-worker/plugin surfaces.
17: 
18: **Core Principle**: Use Cursor for what it does best. Delegate, validate, integrate. The calling AI stays the conductor.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. WHEN TO USE
23: 
24: ### Activation Triggers
25: 
26: - **Cross-AI Validation** — code review second perspective, bug detection, an independent implementation attempt.
27: - **Composer Dispatch** — tasks that specifically want Cursor's own native model (`composer-2.5`/`composer-2.5-fast`), or the Grok (4.5/4.6/4.7) / GLM 5.2 tiers already on the enforced allowlist (see §3 Model Selection).
28: - **Read-Only Exploration** — `--mode plan` (read-only planning) or `--mode ask` (read-only Q&A) when a task wants Cursor's analysis without any file writes.
29: - **Isolated Experimentation** — Cursor's native git worktree isolation (`-w`/`--worktree`) for a change the operator wants tried in a disposable checkout, documented in `references/cursor-tools.md` as an opt-in escape hatch, not this packet's default dispatch shape.
30: - **Specialized Generation** — explicit Cursor requests naming Grok (4.5, 4.6 or 4.7) or GLM 5.2 specifically (the only non-Composer models on the enforced allowlist).
31: 
32: ### When NOT to Use
33: 
34: - **You ARE Cursor already.** If your runtime is `cursor-agent` (detection signal: `CURSOR_AGENT=1` set, `CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID` set, `cursor-agent` in process ancestry, or an active-session probe under `~/.cursor/`), this skill refuses to load. Self-invocation creates a circular dispatch loop and burns tokens for no value.
35: - Simple, quick tasks where CLI overhead is not worth it, or tasks needing an immediate response (auth/network round-trips may delay).
36: - Context already loaded and understood by the current agent.
37: - Interactive refinement requiring the full-screen TUI (use `cursor-agent` directly instead).
38: - Tasks where Cursor CLI is not installed, or the account is not authenticated (`cursor-agent about` reports "Not logged in").
39: 
40: ---
41: 
42: ## 2. SMART ROUTING
43: 
44: The hub's `cli-cursor` mode signal routes a Cursor CLI dispatch here when a request names `cursor-agent`, Composer, a Cursor plan or ask exploration, or Cursor's worktree and cloud-worker surfaces.
45: 
46: `references/cli-reference.md` and `assets/prompt-quality-card.md` load on every invocation; the hub `ROUTER.md` names the mode's first leaves.
47: 
48: Read [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) before selecting skill-local resources and open only the matched files; when nothing matches, report `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` with the checklist there.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## 3. HOW IT WORKS
53: 
54: ### Prerequisites
55: 
56: - Install with `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash` (Windows: `irm 'https://cursor.com/install?win32=true' | iex`).
57: - Authenticate `cli-cursor` through **Cursor account OAuth**. Run `cursor-agent login` and complete the browser flow.
58: - `NO_OPEN_BROWSER` disables browser opening for headless hosts.
59: - Use `CURSOR_API_KEY` or `--api-key` for headless/CI auth.
60: - Full install, auth, flag, hook, and unique-surface tables are in the ALWAYS-loaded [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md).
61:   This section keeps only the routing decisions and dispatch-critical gotchas.
62: 
63: ### Execution Ownership
64: 
65: This packet owns:
66: - user-facing routing,
67: - the `command -v cursor-agent` availability probe,
68: - prompt construction, and
69: - the self-invocation guard.
70: 
71: Research and review lineages delegate process construction and execution to the already-shipped deep-loop runtime at `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs`, using executor kind `cli-cursor`.
72: That runner accepts only the `research` and `review` loop types.
73: For a single build or doc dispatch, use the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5.
74: 
75: The runtime is the single Cursor execution adapter. Do not add a packet-local wrapper, command builder, or spawn path. Direct `cursor-agent -p` snippets below are operator reference and manual-testing examples; research and review lineages use the shared runtime, and a one-shot dispatch uses the child envelope.
76: 
77: ### Provider Auth Pre-Flight
78: 
79: **MANDATORY before any first dispatch in a session.** `cursor-agent -p` without a valid session exits `0` even on an auth failure — the exit code is never a reliable availability signal. Run this check once per session, cache the result, and re-run it only if a dispatch's output text (not its exit code) shows an authentication error.
80: 
81: ```bash
82: # One-shot pre-flight: capture account auth status for routing
83: CURSOR_ABOUT=$(cursor-agent about 2>&1)
84: echo "$CURSOR_ABOUT" | grep -qi "not logged in" && CURSOR_AUTH_OK=0 || CURSOR_AUTH_OK=1
85: ```
86: 
87: **Decision tree** (apply in order — first match wins):
88: 
89: | State | CURSOR_AUTH_OK | Action |
90: |-------|-----------------|--------|
91: | Authenticated | 1 | Proceed with `cursor-agent -p "<prompt>" --output-format text --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled` |
92: | Not logged in | 0 | **ASK user** to run `cursor-agent login` — surface the command, do NOT dispatch. Never substitute an unrelated CLI. |
93: 
94: **User prompt template — not logged in:**
95: 
96: ```
97: Cursor CLI is not authenticated on this machine. cli-cursor uses Cursor account OAuth
98: (or CURSOR_API_KEY for headless auth). Run `cursor-agent login`
99: (browser flow), then confirm when login finishes — the skill will retry the original dispatch.
100: ```
101: 
102: **Error-recovery contract.** If a dispatch's output text shows an auth error after pre-flight passed (session expired or revoked), invalidate the cache, re-run the pre-flight, and re-check before retrying. Never substitute a model the user didn't approve.
103: 
104: ### Model Selection — Enforced Allowlist
105: 
106: The cli-cursor dispatch is scoped to exactly 29 ids.
107: Never dispatch a model outside the allowlist, including `auto`.
108: Never substitute the closest-sounding allowed model without telling the user.
109: Default to `composer-2.5`.
110: Choose a Gemini 3.8 Flash High / GLM 5.2 / GPT-5.6 Luna Max / Grok (4.5, 4.6 or 4.7) tier only when the task or user explicitly names that family.
111: Cursor has no `--reasoning-effort` flag and rejects parameterized model brackets outright.
112: Select effort tiers through exact enumerated ids.
113: 
114: The enforced allowlist (29 ids) and per-task rationale table are inline in [references/cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md) §5 and [references/providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §2.
115: The runtime layer enforces it through `CURSOR_SUPPORTED_MODELS` in `executor-config.ts`.
116: `fanout-run.cjs` and `dispatch-model.cjs` check it before constructing any command. This skill enforces it too.
117: If a task needs a model outside the allowlist, escalate to the user rather than fabricating a substitute or falling back to `auto`.
118: 
119: ### Default Invocation (Skill Default)
120: 
121: **Default model + approval**: `composer-2.5` (Cursor's own native model) · `auto-review` approval (Smart Auto). `auto` (Cursor's own router) is NOT used — it can silently resolve to a model outside the enforced allowlist above, which defeats the point of enforcing one.
122: 
123: > **Fan-out fallback:** a deep-loop lineage that pins no model runs **Composer**. The family is named here on purpose, without a version or an effort tier, so this line does not go stale when the family ships a point release; the runner resolves the current id. A drift test keeps the two in the same family.
124: 
125: ```bash
126: cursor-agent -p "<prompt>" \
127:   --output-format text \
128:   --model composer-2.5 \
129:   --auto-review \
130:   --sandbox enabled
131: ```
132: 
133: **User override** (honor explicit user phrasing verbatim, but ONLY within the enforced allowlist — see Model Selection above):
134: 
135: | User says | Resolve to |
136: |-----------|------------|
137: | (nothing specified) | `--model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled` |
138: | "Use Composer" | `--model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled` |
139: | "Use Composer fast" | `--model composer-2.5-fast --auto-review --sandbox enabled` |
140: | "Use Composer max" / "Composer Max Mode" | Composer has no `-max` (1M "Max Mode") tier — only `composer-2.5`/`composer-2.5-fast`. Tell the user; do not substitute another model's `-max`. |
141: | "Use Grok" / "Grok high" | `--model cursor-grok-4.6-high --auto-review --sandbox enabled` |
142: | "Use Grok 4.7" / "Grok 4.7 high" | `--model grok-4.7-high --auto-review --sandbox enabled` |
143: | "Use GLM" / "GLM max" | `--model glm-5.2-max --auto-review --sandbox enabled` |
144: | "Just plan it, don't write anything" | `--model composer-2.5 --mode plan` (read-only; approval flags do not apply in plan mode) |
145: | "Full auto, run everything" | `--model composer-2.5 --force --sandbox disabled` |
146: | Any model NOT in the allowlist (e.g. "GPT-5.2 high", "use auto") | **Refuse the model, do not substitute silently.** Tell the user this dispatch is scoped to the allowlist above and ask which allowed model to use instead. |
147: 
148: Honor whichever dimensions the user names (approval level, mode). Model stays on `composer-2.5` unless the user explicitly names a different ALLOWED model.
149: 
150: ### Cursor Agent Delegation
151: 
152: The calling AI is the conductor.
153: Cursor's own skill system at `~/.cursor/skills-cursor/` confirms live that Cursor supports subagents natively.
154: Its skills include:
155: - `automate`, `babysit`, `canvas`, `create-hook`, `create-rule`, `create-skill`, `create-subagent`, `loop`, `migrate-to-skills`, `sdk`, `shell`, `split-to-prs`, `statusline`, `update-cli-config`, and `update-cursor-settings`.
156: 
157: These are Cursor-editor-side conventions, not a `-p <profile>` flag like Codex's.
158: Find the full delegation contract and the `--mode plan`/`--mode ask`/default-agent execution-mode roster in [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md).
159: 
160: #### Custom Subagents (CORRECTION -- earlier claim was wrong)
161: 
162: An earlier pass recorded that "`cursor-agent --help` has no custom-agent-loading concept." **That was wrong**, and the error is instructive: agent profiles are discovered by *file convention*, never by a CLI flag, so grepping `--help` for a flag proves nothing about whether the concept exists.
163: 
164: Cursor CLI loads custom subagents from two places, confirmed live:
165: 
166: | Source | Scope | Status here |
167: |--------|-------|-------------|
168: | `.cursor/agents/*.md` | project | This repo mirrors all 11 roster agents here |
169: | `.claude/agents/*.md` | project (Claude-format auto-import) | Already worked before any mirror existed |
170: 
171: Cursor's own bundled `create-subagent` skill documents the format:
172: - Both `name` and `description` frontmatter fields are required.
173: - The Markdown body is the system prompt.
174: 
175: A live `cursor-agent --force -p` roster probe lists all 11 repo agents alongside Cursor's own built-ins:
176: `ai-council`, `code`, `context`, `debug`, `deep-research`, `deep-review`, `design`, `markdown`, `orchestrate`, `prompt-improver`, and `review`.
177: The probe found no duplicate entries when both sources define the same name.
178: 
179: Each `.cursor/agents/<name>.md` is a **symlink** to the canonical `.claude/agents/<name>.md`.
180: This matches the discovery-mirror precedent already used for `.claude/hooks/` and `.codex/hooks/`.
181: There is one source of truth, so a mirror can never drift from the agent it mirrors.
182: 
183: Note: `~/.cursor/agents/` (user-level) is documented by Cursor but a live probe found the CLI did **not** load a profile placed there; only the project-level paths above are verified working. Dispatch remains subject to this repo's own `preToolUse` spec-gate, which is correct behavior.
184: 
185: ### Repository Rules, Hook Delivery, and Parity Boundaries
186: 
187: Cursor CLI reads project `.cursor/rules/*.md`, root `AGENTS.md`, root `CLAUDE.md`, and legacy `.cursorrules` automatically. This repo now uses `.cursor/rules/skill-routing.md` as a compact, always-on pointer to the relevant top-level `.skilled/skills/*/SKILL.md` packets. It is static session context, not a replacement for dynamic per-turn classification.
188: 
189: The `beforeSubmitPrompt` adapter is designed to deliver a dynamic skill-advisor-equivalent brief.
190: Delivery is confirmed dormant under the installed Cursor CLI build.
191: Its source marks the status as registered but unconfirmed and records the shared-advisor delegation in [`user-prompt-submit.ts`](../../system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/cursor/user-prompt-submit.ts#L5-L14) and [`user-prompt-submit.ts`](../../system-spec-kit/runtime/hooks/cursor/user-prompt-submit.ts#L45-L51).
192: A live marker re-probe against `cursor-agent 2026.07.23-e383d2b` confirmed that `beforeSubmitPrompt` did not fire.
193: The static rules file therefore complements a missing dynamic brief.
194: It does not claim to provide per-turn advisor output.
195: The hook registration and adapter remain unchanged.
196: 
197: `cursor-agent --help` has no native command-roster listing subcommand. This repository still exposes a `.cursor/commands/` parity surface: the synchronizer derives it from eligible `.skilled/commands/` files, excludes `goal-opencode.md`, and adds the runtime-native `goal-cursor.md`; validate membership with `command-scope.cjs` and validate behavior with a real slash-command invocation.
198: 
199: | Task Type | Execution mode |
200: |-----------|-----------------|
201: | Code review / bug detection | default agent, `--sandbox enabled` |
202: | Read-only exploration / architecture questions | `--mode ask` |
203: | Multi-step planning without writes | `--mode plan` |
204: | Code generation / file edits | default agent, `--auto-review` or `--force` |
205: 
206: ### Dispatch-Critical Gotchas
207: 
208: The full flag glossary, hook contract, shared-config surface, and troubleshooting table are in the ALWAYS-loaded [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md). Gotchas that silently break a dispatch and must be honored at routing time:
209: 
210: - **The exit code is never an availability signal.** `cursor-agent -p` without auth exits `0` and prints an error to stdout/stderr instead. Every guard and pre-flight in this packet checks output text, never exit code.
211: - **The canonical binary is `cursor-agent`, never the bare `agent` alias.** `agent` is a symlink to the same binary; using it in a process-ancestry match risks colliding with an unrelated `agent` command.
212: - **Cursor shares its entire config surface with the Cursor editor** (`.cursor/`/`~/.cursor/`: `mcp.json`, `hooks.json`, `rules/`, `cli-config.json`). A dispatched `cursor-agent` silently inherits the operator's shared hooks/MCP/rules unless a workspace/config-isolation flag is used — see [shared-editor-config.md](./references/shared-editor-config.md).
213: - **No `model[effort=...]` bracket support.** Unlike some sibling CLIs' parameterized model syntax, `cursor-agent --model 'cursor-grok-4.6[effort=high]'` is rejected outright ("Cannot use this model") — effort tiers must be selected via an exact enumerated id (`cursor-grok-4.6-high`), never a bracket.
214: - **`--auto-review`/`--force` are the write-capable escalation, not `--sandbox`.** `--sandbox enabled|disabled` toggles the OS-level sandbox; the approval decision (whether unattended actions run without a human) is `--auto-review` (Smart Auto) or `--force`/`--yolo` (Run Everything) — omitting both leaves Cursor's own prompt-and-block default in place, which cannot proceed unattended.
215: - **Project-scoped MCP servers show `not loaded (needs approval)`** until trusted. For a non-interactive dispatch that needs MCP tools, add `--approve-mcps` to the `cursor-agent -p` command (auto-approves configured MCP servers for that run); for a persistent operator grant use `cursor-agent mcp enable <server>` (a trust mutation the automation itself must never run).
216: 
217: ---
218: 
219: ## 4. RULES
220: 
221: ### ✅ ALWAYS
222: 
223: 1. Verify Cursor CLI is installed before first invocation (`command -v cursor-agent`).
224: 2. Delegate research and review lineages to `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs` with executor kind `cli-cursor`. It rejects every other loop type, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5. Never build a second adapter in this packet.
225: 3. Use `--mode plan` or `--mode ask` for read-only exploration/analysis/research; use the default agent mode with `--auto-review` or `--force` for code generation/file modification.
226: 4. Validate Cursor-generated code (XSS, injection, eval, syntax checks via `node --check`, `tsc --noEmit`, etc.) before applying.
227: 5. Capture stderr (`2>&1`) so errors surface; check output TEXT for auth/availability failures, never the exit code (always `0`).
228: 6. **Redirect cursor-agent stdin from `/dev/null` on EVERY non-interactive dispatch** — not only inside a `while read` loop, which is the condition this rule used to name and the reason it was skipped, mirroring the family-wide convention: `cursor-agent -p "$PROMPT" > "$LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null &`. Live-verified: a real `cursor-agent -p ... </dev/null` dispatch completes normally with no hang.
229: 7. **Specify model and approval mode explicitly** — never rely on caller environment. Default: `--model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled`. Honor user overrides verbatim, but ONLY within the enforced allowlist (§3 Model Selection) — never `auto`, never a model outside the 29 allowed ids.
230: 8. Route to `--mode plan`/`--mode ask`/default agent per the task type (see Section 3 routing table).
231: 9. **Pass the spec folder to the delegated agent** in the prompt: if the calling AI has an active Gate-3 spec folder, include `Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)`. If none, ASK the user before delegating — the delegated agent cannot answer Gate 3 in `--force`/non-interactive mode.
232: 10. **Prompt construction & model-craft (cli-* family precedence).** Compose every dispatch prompt via the 2-tier rule canonical in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md`:
233:    1. **Fast path (default).** Build from the local `assets/prompt-quality-card.md`, which delegates the framework table + CLEAR check to the canonical card.
234:    2. **Deep path (escalation).** Dispatch `@prompt-improver` via the Task tool (never load full `sk-prompt` inline) when any canonical **Tier 2** trigger applies — the trigger list lives in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` under "Tier 2 — Deep path"; do not re-enumerate it here.
235: 11. **Never inject user-level voice/personalization content into AI-orchestrated Cursor delegations.** Cursor CLI reads rules from `.cursor/rules`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and legacy `.cursorrules` automatically. When an AI delegates via `cursor-agent -p`, the calling AI's own voice rules govern the response — keep delegations focused on task/model/approval/(spec-folder pre-approval).
236: 12. **Code Standards Loading (surface-aware contract)** — When dispatching for code review or code generation, instruct the dispatched session to:
237:     1. Load `sk-code`.
238:     2. Let `sk-code` emit a surface tag matching the detected stack from markers and target files.
239:     3. Load the selected surface resources and run its verification commands.
240:     4. Add `code-review` only for formal findings-first review output.
241: 
242:     Fallback: if the surface cannot be determined confidently, ask for the runtime surface and verification command set.
243:     NEVER hardcode obsolete sibling code skills in dispatch prompts.
244: 13. **Design Standards Loading (measured-reference contract)** — When dispatching for design or UI work, instruct the dispatched session to:
245:     1. Load `sk-design-md-generator`.
246:     2. Extract a measured Style Reference DESIGN.md from the live source before building UI. Include named color tokens, type scale, components, and Quick-Start CSS/Tailwind.
247:     3. Build against those measured tokens and run the extraction's validate step to confirm hex/section fidelity.
248: 
249:     Fallback: if there is no live source to measure, ask for the reference URL or the exact tokens to build against.
250:     NEVER treat `mcp-figma` or `sk-design-md-generator` as a taste, visual-direction, or critique authority.
251:     The extraction measures real CSS; it does not judge design.
252: 14. **Pass the design reference manifest to the dispatched session** — when dispatching design or UI work, inline a `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST v1` block in the prompt.
253:     The child cannot resolve skill paths, so the manifest travels in the payload, not by reference.
254:     Include `styleReferenceExtracted` true, the live `source` that was measured, the measured design tokens / type scale / components the child must build against, `loadedFiles`, and `proofDemandBack`.
255:     If the manifest cannot be assembled because no Style Reference was extracted or no live source can be measured, ASK before launching the child rather than starting a silent design dispatch.
256:     The child returns the demanded proof, and the parent reconciles it on the return path.
257: 15. **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped).**
258:     - By default, launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family.
259:     - Wait for the dispatched agent's work to return and verify that outputs exist.
260:       Then SIGKILL only the dispatch THIS skill started. Capture its PID at launch with `cursor-agent -p ... & CURSOR_PID=$!`.
261:       Kill that PID directly and its own orphan children with `kill -9 "$CURSOR_PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$CURSOR_PID" 2>/dev/null`.
262:     - **Never use a blanket `pkill -9 -f "cursor-agent"` pattern.** It matches and kills EVERY running `cursor-agent` process on the machine, including the operator's unrelated Cursor sessions and the operator's own Cursor editor, since the CLI shares the binary family.
263:     - Launch the next dispatch, this skill or a sibling, only after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped.
264:     - **Within a deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research), the operator authorizes the whole multi-iteration session at the start.
265:       Iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration confirmation prompt.
266:     - **Exception (cross-skill parallel):** when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently.
267:       Still SIGKILL each by its own captured PID as its work returns.
268: 16. **Set `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` in the dispatched child's env and state the exemption in the prompt.**
269:     The variable makes the waiver true, but it does not make it observable.
270:     The reader being waived is a model, and a model cannot see an environment variable.
271:     A child given only the variable still stops to ask the documentation-scope question and writes nothing, at exit code zero.
272:     Copy the preamble from [`shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md`](../shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md) to the top of every non-interactive prompt.
273:     A session may be launched through the per-session worktree wrapper (`.skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh`).
274:     A dispatched `cursor-agent -p` is an orchestrated sub-session, not a new top-level session.
275:     It must SHARE the parent's worktree rather than allocate its own.
276:     This is distinct from Cursor's own native `-w` worktree flag, which this packet's default dispatch never passes.
277:     Pattern: `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 cursor-agent -p ... </dev/null`.
278:     This is harmless when the wrapper is not in use.
279:     See `.skilled/bin/README.md` → "Worktree session isolation".
280: 
281: 17. **Agent-persona injection (attach identity, not just the task).**
282:     Every dispatch composes `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}`, never a bare task.
283:     Resolve the persona from the ACTIVE runtime's agent directory per AGENTS.md §9:
284:     `.cursor/agents/<name>.md`, `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, `.skilled/agents/<name>.md`, and other runtime paths.
285:     Never hardcode one runtime.
286:     Map each subtask to the RIGHT agent, not one default:
287:     `code`→code, `review`→review, `design`→design, research→`deep-research`, and docs→`markdown`.
288:     **Cursor has a native file-convention subagent surface.**
289:     `.cursor/agents/*.md` and `.claude/agents/*.md` mirror all 13 canonical agents.
290:     Dispatch by naming the resolved subagent to satisfy the rule.
291:     On a bare `cursor-agent -p` that names no subagent, **INLINE** the persona block into the payload.
292:     Use the same in-payload pattern as the `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST` (Rule 14), because the child cannot resolve agent paths by reference.
293:     A persona-less dispatch runs the leaf as a generic assistant and silently drops the agent's tool-scope, verification gates, and output contract.
294:     The canonical contract is `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection".
295:     The native precedent is `orchestrate.md` "Agent Loading Protocol".
296:     Declare rare exceptions at the dispatch site: a native surface used, a focused summary for a small-context model, or a pure-mechanical command.
297: 
298: ### ⛔ NEVER
299: 
300: 1. Pass `-w`/`--worktree` or dispatch `cursor-agent worker` from orchestrated fan-out without explicit user approval — these are opt-in escape hatches documented in `references/cursor-tools.md`, not this packet's default dispatch behavior.
301: 2. Trust Cursor output blindly for security-sensitive code, send sensitive data (API keys, passwords, credentials) in prompts, or hammer the CLI with rapid sequential calls.
302: 3. Use Cursor for tasks where context is already loaded — direct action by the calling AI is faster.
303: 4. Assume Cursor output is correct without verification — cross-reference codebase and project standards.
304: 5. Build or maintain a packet-local Cursor execution adapter; the deep-loop runtime is the execution authority.
305: 6. Treat a `0` exit code as proof of a successful, authenticated dispatch — always inspect output text.
306: 7. Do not dispatch a `--model` value outside the enforced 29-id allowlist (§3 Model Selection), including `auto`.
307:    Do not silently substitute the closest-sounding allowed model instead of asking the user.
308:    The runtime layer enforces this through `CURSOR_SUPPORTED_MODELS`/`isCursorModelAllowed` in `executor-config.ts`.
309:    A hard-rejecting check also runs in `fanout-run.cjs`'s `buildCursorLineageCommand` and `dispatch-model.cjs`'s cli-cursor case.
310:    This rule states the same constraint for advisory/manual dispatches the runtime layer cannot see.
311: 
312: ### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
313: 
314: 1. Cursor CLI is not installed and user has not acknowledged (provide `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash`).
315: 2. `cursor-agent about` reports "Not logged in" and the user has not acknowledged running `cursor-agent login`.
316: 3. Cursor output conflicts with existing code patterns (present both perspectives; user decides).
317: 4. Task requests `cursor-agent worker` (cloud execution) or native worktree isolation (`-w`) as part of an orchestrated fan-out (describe the scope-creep risk; get explicit user approval).
318: 
319: ### Memory Handback Protocol
320: 
321: When you need to preserve session context from a Cursor CLI delegation, run the canonical procedure:
322: - Extract the `MEMORY_HANDBACK` section.
323: - Build structured JSON and scrub secrets.
324: - Invoke `generate-context.js` via `--stdin`/`--json`/temp-file.
325: 
326: The continuity writer is the last step. Nothing is handed to an index.
327: Find the full procedure and caveats in [ `system-spec-kit/references/cli/memory-handback.md`](../../system-spec-kit/references/cli/memory-handback.md).
328: Use the Cursor-specific Memory Epilogue template in [assets/prompt-templates.md](./assets/prompt-templates.md).
329: 
330: ```bash
331: printf '%s' "$JSON_PAYLOAD" | node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js --stdin [spec-folder]
332: ```

15: 
16: # Cursor CLI - Complete Command Reference
17: 
18: Reach for this file when a flag is unclear, a dispatch fails on auth or trust, or a model id needs checking against the enforced allowlist.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: Provide a comprehensive, single-source reference for all Cursor CLI commands, flags, models, configuration options, and troubleshooting guidance.
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: - Setting up or configuring Cursor CLI
31: - Looking up command-line flags or subcommands
32: - Troubleshooting authentication or dispatch issues
33: - Selecting the right model or execution mode for a task
34: - Understanding the shared editor-config surface before a dispatch
35: 
36: ### Core Principle
37: 
38: Cursor CLI (`cursor-agent`) is a terminal-based AI coding agent from Cursor, distinct from the Cursor editor but sharing its entire config surface. It dispatches non-interactively via `-p`; this skill defaults dispatch to `composer-2.5` (Cursor's own model) and enforces a 29-id allowlist — Cursor's own `auto` router is deliberately excluded (§5). Unlike sibling CLIs, Cursor has no `--reasoning-effort` flag and no `model[effort=...]` bracket support — effort tiers are baked into the model id itself.
39: 
40: ### Key Sources
41: 
42: | Source | URL |
43: |--------|-----|
44: | **Docs** | [Cursor CLI docs](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/overview) |
45: | **Install** | [Install script](https://cursor.com/install) |
46: | **Account** | [Cursor account](https://cursor.com) |
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## 2. INSTALLATION
51: 
52: | Method | Command | Notes |
53: |--------|---------|-------|
54: | **Install script (macOS/Linux)** | `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS \| bash` | Downloads the platform-matched binary; installs to `~/.local/bin` |
55: | **Install script (Windows)** | `irm 'https://cursor.com/install?win32=true' \| iex` | PowerShell installer |
56: | **Verify** | `cursor-agent --version` | Prints the installed build (e.g. `2026.07.23-e383d2b`) |
57: 
58: **Binary naming**: the canonical on-PATH binary is `cursor-agent`; `agent` is an alias symlink to the same binary. Scripts and process-ancestry checks must probe `command -v cursor-agent`, never assume a bare `agent` command.
59: 
60: **Platform support:**
61: 
62: | Platform | Status |
63: |----------|--------|
64: | macOS (arm64/x86_64) | Full support |
65: | Linux | Full support |
66: | Windows | Supported via the win32 install script |
67: 
68: After installation, run `cursor-agent` for the interactive mode or `cursor-agent -p "prompt"` for non-interactive use.
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ## 3. AUTHENTICATION
73: 
74: cli-cursor authenticates through **Cursor account OAuth** — `cursor-agent login` (browser flow; `NO_OPEN_BROWSER=1` disables automatic browser opening for headless hosts).
75: 
76: **OAuth login/logout/status:**
77: 
78: ```bash
79: # Authenticate via Cursor account (opens browser)
80: cursor-agent login
81: 
82: # View authentication status (text output, not a reliable exit code)
83: cursor-agent about
84: 
85: # Log out and clear stored credentials
86: cursor-agent logout
87: ```
88: 
89: **Headless/CI auth:** `CURSOR_API_KEY` env var or `--api-key <key>`. Endpoint override via `--endpoint`/`CURSOR_API_ENDPOINT` (default `https://api2.cursor.sh`); custom headers via `-H`/`--header`.
90: 
91: **Auth-state caveat**: `cursor-agent status` can print a misleadingly cached "Login successful" even when the account is not actually authenticated. `cursor-agent about`'s "User Email" field (or a fail-closed `-p` dispatch's output text) is the reliable check — never trust `status` alone, and never trust the dispatch exit code (always `0`, even on auth failure).
92: 
93: ---
94: 
95: ## 4. COMMAND-LINE FLAGS
96: 
97: ### Essential Flags
98: 
99: | Flag | Values | Description |
100: |------|--------|-------------|
101: | `-p` / `--print` | (none) | Non-interactive/print mode — required for orchestrated dispatch |
102: | `--output-format` | `text`, `json`, `stream-json` | `text` (default, final-answer-only), `json` (structured, includes `session_id`), `stream-json` (message-level progress) |
103: | `--stream-partial-output` | (none) | Pairs with `stream-json` for text deltas |
104: | `--model` | one of 29 allowed ids (see §5) | Model to use — `auto` and every other Cursor id are rejected by this skill's dispatch layer |
105: | `--mode` | `plan`, `ask` | `plan` = read-only planning; `ask` = read-only Q&A; omit for the default read-write agent mode (`--plan` is a shorthand for `--mode plan`) |
106: | `--force` / `-f` / `--yolo` | (none) | "Run Everything" — auto-approves unless explicitly denied |
107: | `--auto-review` | (none) | "Smart Auto" — auto-runs safe tool calls, prompts for the rest |
108: | `--sandbox` | `enabled`, `disabled` | Toggles the OS-level sandbox (overrides config) |
109: | `--trust` | (none) | Trusts the workspace without prompting for workspace-trust confirmation |
110: | `--approve-mcps` | (none) | Auto-approves all configured MCP servers |
111: 
112: Headless `--mode plan` guarantees the read-only execution boundary, not a separate numbered-plan artifact on text stdout. Use `--output-format stream-json` when event evidence is required; inspect plan content only when the emitted event payload exposes it.
113: 
114: ### Session & Continuity Flags
115: 
116: | Flag | Description |
117: |------|-------------|
118: | `--resume [chatId]` | Resume a prior chat/session by id |
119: | `--continue` | Continue the most recent session |
120: | `--workspace <path>` | Set the workspace root explicitly |
121: | `--add-dir <path>` | Add an additional accessible directory |
122: | `--plugin-dir <path>` | Add a plugin search directory |
123: 
124: ### Native Worktree Flags (unique surface — see `cursor-tools.md`)
125: 
126: | Flag | Description |
127: |------|-------------|
128: | `-w` / `--worktree [name]` | Start in an isolated git worktree at `~/.cursor/worktrees/<repo>/<name>` |
129: | `--worktree-base <branch>` | Set the base ref for the new worktree |
130: | `--skip-worktree-setup` | Skip setup scripts declared in `.cursor/worktrees.json` |
131: 
132: ### Auth Flags
133: 
134: | Flag | Description |
135: |------|-------------|
136: | `--api-key <key>` | Headless API-key auth |
137: | `-H` / `--header <k:v>` | Custom request header |
138: | `-e` / `--endpoint <url>` | Override the API endpoint |
139: 
140: ### Usage Examples
141: 
142: ```bash
143: # Non-interactive default dispatch
144: cursor-agent -p "Refactor utils.ts to use async/await" --model composer-2.5 --output-format text
145: 
146: # With explicit approval + sandbox
147: cursor-agent -p "Add error handling to auth.ts" --model composer-2.5 --auto-review --sandbox enabled
148: 
149: # Read-only planning
150: cursor-agent -p "Plan a migration to the new API" --mode plan --model composer-2.5
151: 
152: # Read-only Q&A
153: cursor-agent -p "Explain how the retry logic works" --mode ask --model composer-2.5
154: 
155: # Full unattended run
156: cursor-agent -p "Run the test suite and fix failures" --force --sandbox disabled --model composer-2.5
157: 
158: # JSON output (structured, includes session_id)
159: cursor-agent -p "Summarize this module" --output-format json --model composer-2.5
160: ```
161: 
162: ---
163: 
164: ## 5. MODEL SELECTION
165: 
166: **Full model catalog (allowlist mirror + enforcement link + effort explanation) → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md).**
167: 
168: ### Supported Models — Enforced Allowlist
169: 
170: Cursor's live roster spans 150+ hosted-frontier ids (GPT/Claude/Gemini/Grok/GLM/Kimi families, `cursor-agent --list-models`), with no per-model prompt-craft data for almost all of them and ids that drift over time. **cli-cursor dispatch is scoped to exactly 29 ids — this is an enforced allowlist, not a reference list.** `auto` (Cursor's own router) is excluded: it can silently resolve to a model outside this set, defeating the point of enforcing one. Enforced at the runtime layer (`CURSOR_SUPPORTED_MODELS` in `executor-config.ts`; a hard-rejecting check in both `fanout-run.cjs` and `dispatch-model.cjs` before any command is constructed).
171: 
172: Alphabetical by family:
173: 
174: | Family | Allowed ids | Notes |
175: |-------|----|-------|
176: | **Composer** (Cursor-native) ★ default | `composer-2.5`, `composer-2.5-fast` | The direct analog to a provider's own house model — Cursor-exclusive |
177: | **Gemini 3.8** (via Cursor) | `gemini-3.8-flash-high` | Google Gemini 3.8 Flash, High thinking tier only. Cursor displays it as "Gemini 3.8 Flash" — the tier lives in the id suffix; `-low`/`-medium` stay out of scope |
178: | **GLM 5.2** (via Cursor) | `glm-5.2-high`, `glm-5.2-max` | Z.AI's GLM 5.2, 2 tiers |
179: | **GPT-5.6 Luna** (via Cursor) | `gpt-5.6-luna-max`, `gpt-5.6-luna-max-fast` | Max thinking tier only, plus its low-latency `-fast` variant. Other Luna tiers and the Sol/Terra personas stay out of scope |
180: | **Grok 4.5** (via Cursor) | `cursor-grok-4.5-low`, `cursor-grok-4.5-low-fast`, `cursor-grok-4.5-medium`, `cursor-grok-4.5-medium-fast`, `cursor-grok-4.5-high`, `cursor-grok-4.5-high-fast` | xAI's Grok 4.5, 3 thinking tiers, each with a `-fast` variant |
181: | **Grok 4.6** (via Cursor) | `cursor-grok-4.6-low`, `cursor-grok-4.6-low-fast`, `cursor-grok-4.6-medium`, `cursor-grok-4.6-medium-fast`, `cursor-grok-4.6-high`, `cursor-grok-4.6-high-fast`, `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh`, `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh-fast` | xAI's Grok 4.6, all 4 thinking tiers (adds xhigh over 4.5), each with a `-fast` variant |
182: | **Grok 4.7** (via Cursor) | `grok-4.7-low`, `grok-4.7-low-fast`, `grok-4.7-medium`, `grok-4.7-medium-fast`, `grok-4.7-high`, `grok-4.7-high-fast`, `grok-4.7-xhigh`, `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` | xAI's Grok 4.7, all 4 thinking tiers, each with a `-fast` variant. Cursor lists these ids without the `cursor-` prefix the 4.5 and 4.6 ids carry |
183: 
184: Effort tiers are suffixes on the id (`-low`/`-medium`/`-high`/`-xhigh`/`-fast`/`-max`), not a separate flag. Any id NOT in the table above — including `auto`, every Claude and Kimi id, and every non-curated Gemini or GPT-5.6 tier/persona — is out of scope for this skill; escalate to the user rather than dispatching it. Do not read a family name in the table as blanket permission for that family: only the exact ids listed are enforced.
185: 
186: ### Reasoning Effort Configuration
187: 
188: **There is no `--reasoning-effort` flag, and no `model[effort=...]` parameterized bracket support.** Effort is selected by choosing the exact enumerated id with the desired tier suffix (e.g. `cursor-grok-4.6-high` instead of `cursor-grok-4.6` + a bracket); the bracket form is rejected outright with `Cannot use this model`. Full live-tested detail and the id-form footgun → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md) §4.
189: 
190: ### Selection Strategy
191: 
192: | Task Type | Model choice | Rationale |
193: |-----------|-----------------|-----------|
194: | General delegation | `composer-2.5` (default) | Cursor's own model; predictable and always allowed |
195: | Task specifically wants Cursor's own model | `composer-2.5` / `composer-2.5-fast` | Cursor-exclusive, no hosted-provider equivalent |
196: | Task specifically wants Gemini, GLM, GPT-5.6 Luna, or Grok at a tier | An exact allowed id (e.g. `gemini-3.8-flash-high`, `glm-5.2-max`, `gpt-5.6-luna-max`, `cursor-grok-4.6-high`) | Effort is baked into the id; only these 27 non-Composer ids are permitted |
197: | Task wants any model outside the allowlist | **Not supported** | Escalate to the user — do not substitute an allowed model silently |
198: 
199: Always specify `--model` explicitly in scripts for predictability; omitting it defaults to `composer-2.5`, never `auto`.
200: 
201: ---
202: 
203: ## 6. OUTPUT HANDLING
204: 
205: ### Print Mode Output
206: 
207: `cursor-agent -p` writes its final answer to stdout in `text` mode (default). Use `--output-format json` for structured output including `session_id`, `usage`, and `request_id`.
208: 
209: ```bash
210: # Capture to file
211: cursor-agent -p "Generate a TypeScript interface for the User model" \
212:   --model composer-2.5 --output-format text > /tmp/user-interface.ts
213: 
214: # Capture structured JSON (includes session_id)
215: cursor-agent -p "List all exported functions in src/" \
216:   --model composer-2.5 --output-format json > /tmp/result.json
217: jq -r '.result' /tmp/result.json
218: 
219: # Redirect stderr separately
220: cursor-agent -p "Analyze auth flow" --model composer-2.5 > /tmp/analysis.txt 2>/tmp/errors.txt
221: ```
222: 
223: ### Exit Codes
224: 
225: | Code | Meaning |
226: |------|---------|
227: | `0` | Process completed — **NOT proof of success or authentication**; always inspect output text |
228: | Non-zero | A CLI-level failure (e.g. invalid flag) — this is the ONE case exit code is meaningful |
229: 
230: ---
231: 
232: ## 7. WORKSPACE TRUST
233: 
234: Cursor Agent can execute code and access files in the target directory. On an untrusted directory, a dispatch fails with a "Workspace Trust Required" error unless `--trust`, `--yolo`, or `-f` is passed. For orchestrated repo-scoped dispatches inside a repo the operator already trusts, pass `--trust` (or rely on `--force` already implying trust).
235: 
236: ---
237: 
238: ## 8. RULES SOURCES
239: 
240: Cursor CLI reads project rules from multiple sources, applied automatically: `.cursor/rules` (directory), `AGENTS.md` (project root), `CLAUDE.md` (project root), and legacy `.cursorrules`. A dispatched session in this repo picks up `AGENTS.md` at the repo root automatically — relevant when composing a delegation prompt, since the delegated session already has this project's governing rules loaded.
241: 
242: ---
243: 
244: ## 9. MCP INTEGRATION
245: 
246: `cursor-agent mcp` subcommands: `login <id>`, `list`, `list-tools <id>`, `enable <id>`, `disable <id>`.
247: 
248: - **Config files.** `.cursor/mcp.json` (project) or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (user) — "the CLI uses the same configuration as the editor". Precedence: project → global → nested.
249: - **Trust mutation.** `enable <id>` is an operator trust mutation. A configured but unapproved server is a manual-playbook SKIP with blocker `MCP server is configured but not approved; operator must run cursor-agent mcp enable <id> outside playbook`.
250: - **Per-dispatch approval.** `--approve-mcps` auto-approves all configured servers for a dispatch, not for this trust-state inspection.
251: - **Client only.** Cursor CLI is an MCP *client* only — it discovers and uses configured servers; there is no documented mode of it acting as an MCP server itself.
252: 
253: ---
254: 
255: ## 10. SUBCOMMANDS
256: 
257: | Subcommand | Description |
258: |------------|-------------|
259: | `cursor-agent -p "<prompt>"` | Non-interactive execution — runs a single prompt and exits |
260: | `cursor-agent login` / `logout` | Authenticate / clear credentials via Cursor account OAuth |
261: | `cursor-agent status` / `whoami` | Session/account status (caution: `status` can show stale cached state) |
262: | `cursor-agent about` | Reliable account/auth info, including CLI version and login email |
263: | `cursor-agent models` | List available models (requires authentication) |
264: | `cursor-agent mcp <subcommand>` | Manage MCP server connections |
265: | `cursor-agent plugin marketplace` | Manage plugins and plugin marketplaces |
266: | `cursor-agent worker` | Run a private cloud worker (see `cursor-tools.md`) |
267: | `cursor-agent install-shell-integration` / `uninstall-shell-integration` | Manage shell integration |
268: 
269: ---
270: 
271: ## 11. TROUBLESHOOTING
272: 
273: | Problem | Cause | Solution |
274: |---------|-------|----------|
275: | Output contains `Error: Authentication required` (exit `0`) | Not authenticated | Run `cursor-agent login`, or set `CURSOR_API_KEY` |
276: | `cursor-agent status` says "Login successful" but `about` says "Not logged in" | `status` uses a stale cache | Trust `about`'s "User Email" field, not `status` |
277: | `Workspace Trust Required` | Directory not yet trusted | Pass `--trust`, `--yolo`, or `-f` |
278: | `Cannot use this model: <id>[...]` | Parameterized model bracket, not supported | Use an exact enumerated id from `--list-models` |
279: | Task ran but no files changed | `--mode plan`/`--mode ask` used, or neither `--auto-review` nor `--force` was passed | Use the default agent mode with an approval flag for edit tasks |
280: | `command not found: cursor-agent` | Not installed or PATH not updated | `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS \| bash`; verify with `which cursor-agent` |
281: | Unexpected hook fires, or dispatch behaves per operator's editor config | Shared `.cursor/`/`~/.cursor/` config surface | See `shared-editor-config.md` for the isolation implications |
282: | Under `--sandbox enabled`, a dispatched command that calls the skill-advisor CLI gets `degraded: true`, `source: "local-scorer"` and no `freshness` | The CLI answers from its local scorer only when it cannot reach the advisor daemon. The live daemon listens on a Unix socket under `/tmp/system-skill-advisor/`, outside the workspace (resolved by `.skilled/bin/lib/launcher-ipc-bridge.cjs`), and the sandboxed command did not reach it. Three Grok 4.7 dispatches showed this, and the same calls with the sandbox disabled got the live answer | Dispatch with `--sandbox disabled` when the task needs the live advisor answer. Otherwise treat the degraded answer as the sandbox's limit, not an advisor fault |
283: 
284: ---
285: 
286: ## 12. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
287: 
288: | Variable | Purpose |
289: |----------|---------|
290: | `CURSOR_API_KEY` | Headless API-key authentication |
291: | `CURSOR_API_ENDPOINT` | Override the default API endpoint (`https://api2.cursor.sh`) |
292: | `CURSOR_AGENT` | Confirmed live: set to `1` unconditionally whenever the current process runs under `cursor-agent` — the primary self-invocation-guard signal |
293: | `CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID` | Confirmed live: the active session/chat id, matching `--output-format json`'s `session_id` field |
294: | `CURSOR_INVOKED_AS` | Confirmed live: how the binary was invoked (`cursor-agent`) |
295: | `NO_OPEN_BROWSER` | Disables automatic browser opening during `cursor-agent login` |
